title: Nuclear export block of tyrosine-phosphorylated STAT1 facilitates rapid responsiveness to interferon-gamma stimuli at the expense of signal strength.
authors: Meyer, Thomas; Lamprecht, Florian; Begitt, Andreas; Hofer, Thomas; Vinkemeier, Uwe
journal: Biochimica et biophysica acta. Gene regulatory mechanisms
one_liner_zh: 该文用数学模型研究STAT1核质穿梭动力学，虽涉及转录因子STAT1，但聚焦信号转导动态而非DNA结合互作，且方法为常微分方程建模，非AI或物理模拟，与课题核心关联弱。
abstract: Interferon-induced STAT1 (signal transducer and activator of transcription 1) signal transduction constitutes a dynamic network of concurrent activation and inactivation steps that directly transmits extracellular information from the plasma membrane to the nucleus. To elucidate how nuclear retention of tyrosine-phosphorylated STAT1 as a fundamental principle of the STAT1 network directs signal transduction, we have developed a mathematical rate equation model for STAT1 nucleocytoplasmic shuttling. Based on an interplay between experimental data on the behavior of transport variants with altered nucleocytoplasmic translocation and computational simulations, we calculated the mean residence time of phosphorylated STAT1 in the nucleus to be 13.1 min (5%-95%-CI = 1.6-48.4 min), indicating the highly dynamic nature of the STAT1 signal network. However, when we assessed the time course of unphosphorylated STAT1 from nuclear entry to its subsequent cytoplasmic exit, we found that the half-life of nuclear STAT1 in resting cells was even shorter (5.0 min, 5%-95%-CI = 0.3-15.0 min). Our data reveal that the STAT1 pathway has not evolved to achieve maximal signal amplification, but rather allows for a compromise between rapid termination and efficient signal output. Decoupling of nuclear export from its prior dephosphorylation, such that also phospho-STAT1 can unphysiologically exit the nucleus, results in an overall lower nuclear concentration of activated STAT1 throughout the entire stimulation period, demonstrating the physiological significance of the nuclear export block of phosphorylated STAT1 for cytokine-driven signal propagation. Thus, the complex dynamics of the unique STAT1 network accounts for both efficient and flexible signal transduction, particularly in the course of transient stimulation.
abstract_zh: 干扰素诱导的STAT1（信号转导及转录激活因子1）信号转导构成一个由同时进行的激活与失活步骤组成的动态网络，该网络直接将细胞外信息从质膜传递至细胞核。为阐明酪氨酸磷酸化STAT1的核滞留作为STAT1网络的基本原则如何引导信号转导，我们开发了一个描述STAT1核质穿梭的数学速率方程模型。基于对具有改变核质转位能力的转运变体行为的实验数据与计算模拟之间的相互作用，我们计算出磷酸化STAT1在细胞核中的平均停留时间为13.1分钟（5%-95%置信区间 = 1.6-48.4分钟），表明STAT1信号网络具有高度动态性。然而，当我们评估非磷酸化STAT1从核进入至随后胞质排出的时间进程时，发现静息细胞中核STAT1的半衰期甚至更短（5.0分钟，5%-95%置信区间 = 0.3-15.0分钟）。我们的数据揭示，STAT1通路并非进化以实现最大信号放大，而是允许在快速终止与高效信号输出之间达成折衷。将核输出与其先前的去磷酸化解偶联，使得磷酸化STAT1也能非生理性地离开细胞核，导致整个刺激期间激活STAT1的核浓度总体降低，这证明了磷酸化STAT1的核输出阻断对细胞因子驱动的信号传播的生理学意义。因此，独特STAT1网络的复杂动力学既保证了高效又灵活的信号转导，尤其是在瞬时刺激过程中。
